bullets.text: AKIEN'S SENTENCE IS THE NODE: 'the questions are the sieve.' It dissolves the contradiction he opened with — a learning block's anatomy names a KB and constraining questions and never says WHERE they live, so a rigid dict of questions is a legal KB and build_inspector was never disqualified by having one. What actually disqualifies it is that it does not run on the engine at all.

MEASURED AT CAST, and it shrank the work: learning_block/engine.py:169 collects killed_by as a LIST across every constraint in one pass. One shake and the gradation are ALREADY BUILT in the evaluation loop. The nest's only missing piece is banding plus the not-applicable value — a small change in learning_block, not a new mechanism in build_inspector.

THE DERIVATION IS THE POINT, in Akien's words: the mesh is 'a charactaristic of the kind of thing it's doing rather than where it's doing it. greater reusability.' A sieve knows nothing about its nest and the nest reads nothing but the sieve's own code, so there is no configuration surface between them — and the ordering cannot go stale, because a sieve that starts reaching further drops a band on its own at the next derivation. A hand-labeled nest would keep it near the top and nobody would notice.

BANDS, NOT NUMBERS, and the boundaries are where the FAILURE MODE changes, not where the milliseconds do: input-in-hand cannot fail environmentally; local disk fails on absence; correlated local work fails on inconsistency; off-box fails on UNAVAILABILITY, which nothing above it can do. That last boundary is the one that earns its keep — an unreachable host must never be able to mask a local finding, and banding makes that structurally impossible. Strict numbering was rejected on ownership: inserting a sieve between 2 and 3 is a WRITE TO ITS NEIGHBOURS (Law 6), and bands have no such problem.

CC REIFIED AN EXAMPLE AGAIN, caught by Akien at n=1 in this session: his mesh example (exists -> non-empty -> valid JSON -> field present -> in range) was an ILLUSTRATION of asking the finest question that answers the need, and CC shipped it as a five-tier taxonomy and a definition of coarseness. Same tell as the trigger-kinds enum and the rack. The correction also produced the better axis, which was his: coarseness is PROXIMITY — how deep do we have to look — not computation time.

THIS NODE IS THE TEST tickets/learning-block-engine-track SAID IT WAS WAITING FOR. Its wrong-intent tell is 'if a second block requires per-block special cases inside the engine, the one-engine hypothesis is falsified.' build_inspector is that second block. The watch is bound to exactly that, and a demanded branch is a spec-changing input for Akien rather than a detail to route around.

UNRESOLVED AND NAMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY: whether a tri-valued finding fits the shape cairn/base/transitions.py's build gate reads at a journaled crossing. Not checked at cast. It is the one item here that can break the emit chokepoint, so BUILDME opens with it.

OUT OF BOUNDS FOR THIS NODE, stated so it cannot ride along: the filter->sieve rename of ruling 2026-08-06-a-stack-of-sieves-is-a-nest carries its own sequencing clause (before or after nothing-rides-loose, never during). This cast uses the vocabulary and performs no rename.

bullets.text: MEASURED: the ground_loop process started 2026-08-13 15:35:43. Commit ba50814 ('the big bang: 24 components drop one level into their rungs') moved cairn/base/probe.py to cairn/tools/base/probe.py at 20:55 the same evening. For the 29 hours between then and now, fifteen devices carrying twenty-two probes were skipped by the heartbeat.

THE MECHANISM, and it is ordinary Python: discovery.load_module execs each probe file off its path, so the probe binds the CURRENT cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe, while the daemon's own frame still held cairn.base.probe.Probe from before the move. Two distinct class objects wearing one name. isinstance() is an identity test, so it returned False, and the loop reported 'PROBE is Probe, not a Probe' thirteen times.

The two remaining faces are the same staleness from the other side: constrain and orient failed with ImportError for common_shape_record and AmbiguousComponent, both symbols added to cairn.tools.chain.grammar AFTER the process started. One root cause, two error classes, and neither of them names the loop.

THE BENCH MADE IT SELF-SEALING. A benched device is passed to discover() in skip, so it is never re-scanned, its trouble stops recurring, and its count freezes. Four tickets sat at ~10,286 occurrences with last_seen 23.7 hours old — which reads as an outage that ended. It had not ended; it had gone total. An outage that stops recurring is indistinguishable from one that was fixed.

A RESTART ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, which is the trap for whoever meets this next. loop.py:50 defines the bench as 'a live ticket by this name exists', and clearing is the recipient's act alone — so a restarted loop keeps every device dark, silently, with the imports now perfectly fine and nothing red anywhere. The order is restart, verify through the loop's own discover(), then clear.

The predicate that was missing is one comparison and every input to it is already free on disk: is this process older than the code it is judging. Process start time, file mtimes, and the module file behind a class object are all readable, and the check only ever runs on the failure path — so a healthy system pays nothing for it.

For Akien, and it is the part I am least comfortable with: I READ THIS TROUBLE LIST AT SESSION OPEN AND WALKED PAST IT. So did every session before this one. It took building a probe of my own, watching it get benched within a minute, and refusing to accept the message at face value. The list was loud, correctly recorded, and pointed at the wrong party — and being pointed at the wrong party is what made it quiet.

FOUND ONLY BY UN-BENCHING and owed its own ticket, recorded here so it cannot be re-derived: with the watch layer actually armed, probe triggers cost 2531 ms per beat over 22 probes (build_inspector 705, base 1170 across five, inference_domain 566). The beat slowed to ~3.5s against the ruled 5s liveness threshold, so a healthy loop now reads DEAD about a third of the time. The heartbeat had been cheap for 29 hours because it was doing nothing.

signal.verbatim: superseded — staleness detection built and proved, cadence at 60s, incident lessons are in the code
